Hi Laura / Kimberly,

Thanks for the redlines. Procurement asked me to follow up on the indemnity sections specifically — a few items are blocking approval on our side:

- Defense control: your redline currently gives Redwood unilateral right to assume defense. We prefer either mutual control or a requirement that counsel is reasonably acceptable to both parties.
- Scope: need clarity that IP indemnity covers third-party infringement of the unmodified Redwood product, not customer-supplied inputs or customer customizations.
- OSS & training data: our legal team wants an explicit carveout for open-source components and for content that our customers provide.
- Cap & remedies: procurement wants a firm upper bound tied to fees paid under the order form.

Attached is our annotated redline (LegalTrek_redlines_v2.pdf) — highlights in yellow. Can we get a short proposal of options (one page) that we can take back to procurement this afternoon? We are on a tight renewal window; procurement is pushing for sign-off by end of week.

Thanks,
Ravi

Can you draft short language for the compromise option (2) that we can send Ravi — keep it tight: defense control with notice + ability to step in, scope limited to unmodified service, cap = greater of $1M or 12 months' fees, and a cooperation clause. Also include a short paragraph on evidence handoff timeline (we propose 10 business days).

Thanks — Laura

Laura / Ben — drafting suggested language below for the compromise option. Kept it narrow to address procurement asks while protecting Redwood operationally. Please review quickly; I will put into a redline doc if this direction is approved.

Suggested compromise clause (draft):
1) Customer Indemnity (IP). Customer will indemnify, defend and hold harmless Redwood from and against any third-party claim alleging that Customer Content or Customer Modifications infringe a third party's intellectual property rights.
2) Redwood Indemnity (IP). Redwood will indemnify and, at its option, defend Customer against third-party claims that the unmodified Redwood Service infringes a third party's intellectual property rights, provided: (a) Redwood is given prompt written notice of the claim; (b) Customer provides reasonable cooperation and all evidence in Customer's possession; and (c) Redwood has the sole right to control the defense and settlement, provided that Redwood shall not settle any claim that imposes an obligation on Customer without Customer's prior written consent (which will not be unreasonably withheld).
3) Exclusions. The foregoing indemnities shall not apply to claims to the extent arising out of (i) Customer Content; (ii) Customer Modifications; (iii) use of the Service in combination with products, software or data not provided by Redwood; or (iv) open source components as expressly excluded in Schedule X.
4) Cap and Remedies. Redwood's aggregate liability for indemnity obligations shall be limited to the greater of one million US dollars (USD 1,000,000) or the total fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.
5) Evidence and Notice. Customer will provide the evidence listed in Appendix A within ten (10) business days of notice of the claim; failure to do so may affect the allocation of defense costs.

Notes: I tightened the 'sole right to control' language to include a carve for customer consent on settlements that create obligations for the customer. That tends to be compromise-friendly. If Ben wants softer language re: cap, we can move to a fixed multiple of order-form fees instead.

If you both sign off, I'll export as a redline and send to Ravi with the compromise framing.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park

Ravi / Olivia — thanks for the annotated redline and the clarity on procurement's blockers. Attached is a narrowly tailored compromise we hope is acceptable. High level:

- Redwood will accept IP indemnity for the unmodified Service and agrees to assume defense with notice.
- We add an explicit carveout for Customer Content and customer customizations (your ask) and carve out OSS/training-data to the extent identified in Schedule X.
- Cap: greater of $1M or 12 months' fees (we believe this aligns economics and limits tail risk).
- Evidence handoff: 10 business days.

We're trying to balance procurement's need for a cap with our desire to limit exposure on customer-input claims. If procurement needs the cap tied strictly to order-form fees only (no $1M floor), let us know and we'll run the numbers for internal approval — might require Exec sign-off.

Please see attached: Redwood_proposed_redline.docx (redline). If you can confirm whether procurement can accept the OSS carveout as drafted in Schedule X and the $1M floor, we can get legal approvals and prepare signature pages.

Cheers,
Ben
